title: Debugger's expression evaluator does not refresh previous evaluations after 'Step Over'
body:
### Tested versions

Only tested in Godot v4.6.2.stable (Steam's "Default Public Version")

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable (71f334935) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6607) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H (20 threads) - 31.62 GiB memory

### Issue description

Inside Godot's editor, while playing with a debug break into a line, the evaluations in the 'Evaluation' tab does not refresh/update values after steping over, not even if I press the 'Evaluate' button, only if I type the same expression to evaluate again. After that it displays the new value and the previous evaluated expressions update too.

### Steps to reproduce

Full example script:
```gdscript
var some_number: int = 10
some_number = 5
some_number = 99
```
1. Inside Godot's editor, I add a Debug Break into a line
2. Press play
3. The debugger hits line
```gdscript
var some_number: int = 10
```
4. I type some expression into the debugger's Evaluator tab like: ```some_number``` and it displays:
```
some_number |<null>|
```
5. I press Step Over and the debugger hits line
```gdscript
some_number = 5
```
It still displays:
```
some_number |<null>|
```
6. I press the button 'Evalutate' and it still displays:
```
some_number |<null>|
```
7. I type the same expression "```some_number```" in the text input evaluator and only then the new evaluation displays:
```
some_number |5|
some_number |<null>|    <-- previous '<null>' value evaluation stays the same.
```
8. I press Step Over and the debugger hits line
```gdscript
some_number = 99
```
Displays the same as the previous values:
```
some_number |5|
some_number |<null>|
```
9. I write the same expression "```some_number```" again and now displays new values, but update all the previous expressions as well (but not the first null one)
```
some_number |99|
some_number |99|
some_number |<null>|
```

N/A
